mechanism: Use a globally valid Bellman subsolution h on the entire finite pair tree, then raise values only on an active set through one coupled dynamic-dual LP. Inactive pair nodes remain fixed at h, so they stay certified without local OT solves; a feasible policy supplies the root upper bound.
omitted_computation: All local Bellman transport solves and local dual variables at inactive state-pair nodes, plus their successor cross-arcs. Active nodes retain every required successor inequality unless a separate verified group-pricing rule is later added.
assumptions: The target is the corrected finite k-window model in objective.json with an optimized initial coupling and costs at times 1 through T
The baseline h is verified pointwise to satisfy h_t<=T_t h_{t+1}, with h_T=0
Every active value variable is constrained to be at least h, and every active local dual inequality covers all positive successor pairs
Inactive values are exactly h; occupation chooses activation priority only and never deletes an unbounded alternative
The root is represented by an active dummy node whose successor marginals are the two initial laws
Float64 probes test the formulation numerically but do not constitute outward-rounded certification
lemma_or_invariant: Let h be a Bellman subsolution. Fix active sets A_t and define v=h off A and v>=h on A. For every active z=(x,y), if there exist local dual potentials alpha_z,beta_z with v_t(z)<=P_t(x)alpha_z+Q_t(y)beta_z and alpha_z(a)+beta_z(b)<=c_{t+1}(a,b)+v_{t+1}(a,b) for every positive successor pair, then v<=V by backward induction. At an inactive node h_t<=T_t h_{t+1}<=T_t v_{t+1}; at an active node weak OT duality gives v_t<=T_t v_{t+1}. Applying the same construction to the dummy root yields a root lower bound. Any feasible dynamic coupling policy yields an upper bound. With every pair active, the LP has the same optimum as exact backward DP.

prediction: On every case of the frozen short-horizon oracle grid, an exact-optimal-occupation active set plus the dummy root, using the stronger of H=0,1,2 future-marginal subsolutions, attains root relative width<=0.5% while instantiating at most 75% of the successor cross-arc inequalities required by the all-active global LP. Full activation matches exact backward DP within 1e-8 on every correctness fixture.
falsification_rule: Any h-subsolution violation, root lower above exact DP, infeasible recovered policy, or all-active mismatch is implementation_invalid. If the oracle active set is valid but any grid group misses either the 0.5% width or 25% arc-omission threshold, classify the stated active-set performance prediction as falsified; do not infer that every global-dual or pricing scheme is impossible. A successful oracle probe licenses an implementable pricing probe but is not a candidate or SOTA result.

probe.oracle: Independent exact common-model DP retaining optimal conditional plans. Exact occupation selects the active set only in this non-deployable headroom probe and never in a later candidate.
probe.cost_accounting: Primary v2 output is the root certificate gap versus active value variables, dual variables, active successor inequalities, LP nonzeros and same-kernel transport-equivalent work. Count h construction including future marginal propagation and scalar OT, root constraints, exact-oracle work separately, peak memory and wall time. Compare against both the all-active global LP and exact backward DP; no solver timing from this probe is a SOTA speed claim.

absolute and squared non-Monge continuation matrices
full activation versus exact backward DP
probe.stopping: Run the complete 16-case grid and both seeds after theorem/panel review. Candidate never uses the reference value for a deployable stopping rule because this first probe is explicitly oracle-only.

breadth_challenge: The oracle screen crosses both costs, both frozen process families, k=1/2 and coarse/fine deltas. It is deliberately short horizon and small sample count; survival licenses, but cannot replace, T=50 tests at frozen path counts and all three deltas/shifts.
v2_outcome_rule: Passing the oracle probe only licenses a deployable activation/pricing probe. Failing it can stop this defined active-subsolution direction on cost evidence, but cannot establish impossibility for tree algorithms, global dual methods or certification in general. A limited-domain success must remain labelled with its exact restrictions and cannot set scientific_objective_achieved=true.
ablation: Compare h=0, H=1 and H=2; exact-occupation active set versus equal-size deterministic random active sets; active global LP versus the local shared-dual pool using identical float64 LP primitives; and active constraints with versus without time coupling. Report arc omission separately from wall time.
unresolved_objections: The future-marginal h may cost O(H times the number of state pairs) and still be too weak
Active-node successor inequalities can dominate the full DP work even when few pair nodes are active
Exact optimal occupation may be a poor oracle active set because inactive low h values can create alternative cheap policies
The construction overlaps strongly with admissible-heuristic MDP search, occupancy LP and sparse constraint generation; novelty is unestablished
An implementable pricing rule may secretly enumerate every inactive node or successor arc
